So there are things called subatomic particles which make up the structure of an atom. They are protons, neutrons, and electrons. Because they have energy they move and vibrate, as well as spin. They also have inherent charge. Either positive, negative, neutral. A fundamental property of a charge that spins is that it generates a differential energy field around it. That means that due to its charge and spin it generates a field with a different energy at different points in that field. So any charges that move through that field will have a force exerted on them by that field. This force will move the foreign charge to the lowest energy possible. In the same way gravity works to give you potential energy at a height, so too does this field work to give charges potential energy. Imagine each subatomic particle as an arrow. Each arrow points in a direction. Some fields cancel each other out, but not all. So you end up with an atom that has an overall spin. Think a bigger arrow. Now we move to a bulk material that has many atoms. Normally the spins are in many directions so there is no overall magnetic ordering and thus no magnetic field. But, in some materials the arrows all or mostly all point in the same direction. This means that all of those fields work together instead of canceling each other out. This long range magnetic ordering gives you a magnet.

It is important to note that not all things respond to a magnetic field the same way. How they act in a magnet depends on the number, type and spin state of the subatomic particles in the substance. Some are not effected at all by them.

Why is it that moving at a high enough speed alters someone's perception of time? Does this have anything to do with lightspeed being a hard speed limit?

That is exactly the case. No one can travel faster than the speed of light in a vacuum. It all has to do with an enertial reference frame of the observer. Say you have one ship traveling East and another traveling West, both going .99 lightspeed (c). Then common sense tells you that if you are in one ship looking at the other it would appear to be going at 1.98c. In fact this is not the case. They appear to be going about .999c. In order to explain this what has to change is space. This is where space-time dilation and contraction come into play. You change the nature of space when you travel through it at high speed because of your mass (from an outside frame of reference).
